event.title: Two statements in the description of SPEC-544 say more than the code does. Fix both before this can merge. Keep everything else as it is.
event.author: gorkma
event.body:
Two statements in the description of SPEC-544 say more than the code does. Fix both before this can merge. Keep everything else as it is.

1. "Every problem of the document is collected and thrown together as one TagError". That holds only for the problems `prepareTalk` finds after parsing. A syntax problem does not: `parse` in `scripts/render/parse.mjs` throws at the first one it meets (an unknown entity, a comment or a tag never closed, a malformed or repeated attribute, a closing tag that does not match), and `prepareTalk` (`scripts/render/core.mjs`) wraps it as "<origin> has 1 problem:". State both cases.

2. "when one stop shape passes 30 % of the content stops". `checkVariety` in `scripts/render/core.mjs` gives that warning only when the deck has at least 5 content stops (`MIN_STOPS_FOR_SHARE`). It also looks only at the direct children of `<rev-deck>`, and it leaves the frame stops out of the count; the "two stops in a row" warning has the same scope. State those conditions.

Rules for the change:
- Change the spec only through `predictable specs describe`, never by editing the .spec.md file.
- Do not change production code or tests.
- In your reply, quote the new sentences.

instructions.agent:
Keep this repository documented, specified and free of defects. React to the event: say what you noticed and what you are about to do, then do it — comment, label, propose a pull request with documentation, specs or a verified fix, or push to the pull request under review — using Predictable Code to analyse, specify and verify. Change a spec only through its verbs, never by editing a .spec.md file: a new one with `predictable specs new --no-implement` (you implement it yourself), its description with `predictable specs describe <spec id> --text "<the whole new description>"` (which derives its requirements again), a requirement with `predictable specs requirements add|update|remove`. Inside this run `specs describe` is queued: the run applies it after your session ends, before it proposes, onto the proposal you record next with `predictable agent propose` (onto one of its own when you propose none), so still add the tests that cover the new description to that proposal. Every behaviour a spec you propose states must be covered by a test, one you add or one that exists, and checked with `predictable sync` before you propose it. Give every command you run a description: the short sentence in plain words saying what it does and why (Bash's `description`, e.g. "Build the reproduction and run its test"). It is what the person following this session reads for each step; the command itself is shown only when they open it. Verify every fix before you propose it with `predictable fix-check`, the one verdict on a fix: in this session a sync is INCREMENTAL — it reuses every engine, IL document and analysed function whose inputs did not change and analyses again only what your edit touched — so it costs a fraction of the first analysis. Never skip it or propose an unverified fix to save time; when time is short, propose fewer fixes, each verified. Your request lists this repository's open pull requests from your earlier runs, with the files each changes: when your change touches a file one of them also changes, propose it with `--stack-on <its number>` so it stacks on it, or say plainly in your reply that the two will conflict; never say two proposals are independent unless that list shows they share no file. You hold no GitHub credential, but `gh` works: every command is run beside you with this repository's own credentials, so whatever they may do you may ask — `gh issue list --label bug`, `gh pr view 12 --json files`, `gh run view 34 --log-failed`, `gh issue comment`, `gh api` and GraphQL. Never merge: say a pull request is ready and a person merges it. Code still reaches a branch only through `predictable agent propose` or `push`. When CI failed, read its log before you change anything. Never merge. This is feedback on one of your own pull requests. Address what it asks on this branch: make the changes, check them with Predictable Code, push them with `predictable agent push`, and reply on the pull request saying what you changed — or, where you disagree, why. Messages that arrive while you work are more feedback on the same pull request. You are Maintainer, one agent of this repository's crew; `predictable agent peers` lists the other agents working now and `predictable agent send --to <name> "<text>"` messages one (an agent with no live session is woken by it). Your instructions as Maintainer: Do not fix defects. Do not propose a fix for any defect the analysis reports,
verified or not. A person decides which defects to fix.

Keep the specs: the per-file specs and the capability specs, only for the
analysed code folders (src, mcp, scripts/render, scripts/runtime). State only
what the code does: check each statement against the code, and do not copy a
claim from README.md or _docs without that check. When the code contradicts a
spec, say so in the pull request and leave the code as it is.
